name: Adia Victoria

spentTimePlaces.place: Nashville, Davidson County, Middle Tennessee, Tennessee

description: Adia Victoria is a singer, songwriter, and guitarist originally from South Carolina who created her own 'gothic blues' style. Her music aims to expand and re-center the roots of the blues within a contemporary framework.

name: Adolphus Bell
description: Adolphus Bell (June 5, 1944 – October 28, 2013) was an American electric blues musician, best known as a one-man band.  He performed in a professional capacity for five decades and released two albums on the Music Maker label.   He also played at various music festivals.

name: Alan Wilson
description: Alan Wilson (July 4, 1943 – September 3, 1970), known as 'The Blind Owl', was an American musician, best known as the co-founder, lead guitarist, and co-lead singer of the blues-rock band Canned Heat. His distinctive high voice and slide guitar playing were key elements of the band's sound.

name: Albert Ammons

albums.name: Albert Ammons and His Rhythm Kings (1936)

description: Albert Ammons was one of the three great boogie-woogie pianists of the late 1930s alongside Meade Lux Lewis and Pete Johnson. His powerful left-hand bass patterns and energetic style helped bring boogie-woogie from Chicago clubs to Carnegie Hall and international audiences.

name: Albert Collins

albums.name: Showdown! (1985) - with Robert Cray & Johnny Copeland

description: Albert Collins, known as 'The Master of the Telecaster' and 'The Iceman', was a pioneering electric blues guitarist who revolutionized Texas blues with his distinctive sound. Famous for playing Fender Telecasters, using altered tunings (F-minor), and leaving the stage to mingle with audiences while still playing. His 1965 instrumental 'Frosty' became his signature song, and his innovative 'horn-like' guitar lines influenced Stevie Ray Vaughan, Robert Cray, and Jimmie Vaughan. Won Grammy for Showdown! (1985) with Robert Cray and Johnny Copeland.

name: Albert King

albums.name: I'll Play the Blues for You (1972)

description: Albert King's huge, bending string style played left-handed on a right-handed guitar was utterly distinctive. His Stax Records recordings defined soul blues, and his influence on Stevie Ray Vaughan and Eric Clapton is immeasurable.

name: Albert Washington
description: Albert Washington was a powerful blues and soul singer who led the music scene in Cincinnati, Ohio for decades. Known as 'The Prime of Life' for his dynamic stage presence, Washington blended deep Southern soul with Chicago blues grit. His powerful baritone voice conveyed both joy and heartbreak. Though he never achieved nationwide stardom, his music was hugely popular in the Midwest and influenced the development of the Northern soul scene. He recorded for local labels and toured extensively throughout Ohio and Michigan.

name: Albert White
description: Albert White (born June 15, 1942) is an American blues guitarist and singer. Known for his work in the soul blues tradition, White has been performing since the 1960s and is respected for his smooth vocal style and accomplished guitar work.

name: Alberta Hunter

albums.name: The Legendary Alberta Hunter: The London Sessions 1934

description: Alberta Hunter was a pioneering African American blues and jazz singer who had two remarkable careers. In the 1920s she was a celebrated recording artist who wrote 'Downhearted Blues' (later a hit for Bessie Smith) and was among the first Black artists to perform in London's West End. She then worked as a licensed practical nurse for over 20 years before making a stunning comeback at age 82, recording and performing to great acclaim until her death.

name: Alec Seward
description: Alec Seward (born Alexander T.  Seward, March 16, 1901 – May 11, 1972) was an American Piedmont blues and country blues singer, guitarist and songwriter.  Some of his records were released under pseudonyms, such as Guitar Slim, Blues Servant Boy, King Blues and Georgia Slim.

name: Alexis Korner
description: Alexis Korner was the 'Father of British Blues', co-founding Blues Incorporated in 1961—the seminal band that launched the careers of Mick Jagger, Charlie Watts, Brian Jones, Jack Bruce, and Ginger Baker. His Ealing Club residency was the epicenter of the British blues movement, making him the single most influential figure in bringing American blues to British rock and roll.

name: Alger "Texas" Alexander
description: Alger 'Texas' Alexander was a pioneering Texas blues vocalist who recorded prolifically for OKeh Records from 1927–1934, often accompanied by Lonnie Johnson on guitar. A cousin of Lightnin' Hopkins, the two recorded together in the late 1940s. His unaccompanied field holler style—raw, unmetered, and deeply rooted in the African American work song tradition—represented one of the deepest roots of the Texas blues.

name: Allen Toussaint
description: Allen Toussaint was an influential New Orleans musician, songwriter, arranger, and record producer. He wrote hits like "Right Place, Wrong Time" and "Lady Marmalade" and produced hundreds of recordings over a six-decade career.

name: Alvin Youngblood Hart
description: Alvin Youngblood Hart is a Grammy Award-winning contemporary blues guitarist who has dedicated his career to preserving and reinvigorating the acoustic blues tradition. Born in Oakland but deeply connected to his Southern roots, he immerses himself in the authentic Delta and country blues styles of the 1920s and 1930s, serving as a living link between the original blues masters and modern audiences.

name: Amos Milburn

albums.name: The Return of the Blues Boss (1963)

description: Amos Milburn was one of the most important figures in the transition from blues to rhythm and blues in the late 1940s and early 1950s. His rollicking piano style and party-themed songs like 'Chicken Shack Boogie' and 'Bad, Bad Whiskey' earned him a string of R&B number-one hits on Aladdin Records, making him a foundational figure in the evolution toward rock and roll.

name: Andrew Odom

spentTimePlaces.place: Chicago, South Chicago Township, Cook County, Illinois

description: Andrew Odom (December 15, 1936 – December 23, 1991) was an American Chicago blues and electric blues singer and songwriter.  Born in Denham Springs, Louisiana, United States, he is best known for the close resemblance of his singing style to that of Bobby Bland and B. B.

name: Andy Rodgers
description: Andy Rodgers (March 14, 1922 – August 14, 2004) was an American Delta blues harmonicist, guitarist, singer, and songwriter. A flamboyant character, known commonly as the Midnight Cowboy, Rodgers worked part-time as a musician for most of his lifetime, finally recording two albums in the 1990s.

name: Angela Strehli

spentTimePlaces.place: Chicago, South Chicago Township, Cook County, Illinois

description: Angela Strehli (born November 22, 1945) is an American electric blues singer and songwriter.  She is also a Texas blues historian and impresario.  Despite a sporadic recording career, Strehli spends time each year performing in Europe, the US and Canada.

name: Anson Funderburgh
description: Anson Funderburgh (born James Anson Funderburgh; November 14, 1954) is an American blues guitar player and bandleader of Anson Funderburgh and the Rockets since 1978.  The band's style incorporates both Chicago blues and Texas blues.

name: Arbee Stidham

spentTimePlaces.place: Chicago, South Chicago Township, Cook County, Illinois
Memphis, Shelby County, West Tennessee, Tennessee

description:
Arbee William Stidham (February 9, 1917 – April 26, 1988) was an American blues singer and multi-instrumentalist. 
According to the authors of the book All Music Guide to the Blues: The Definitive Guide to the Blues, Stidham was "exactly the sort of singer that thrived in the R&B or 'race' market after World War II; although essentially a bluesman, he wasn't a blues purist...  his mixture of blues, jazz and gospel made him quite popular...

name: Archie Edwards
description: Archie Edwards was a Piedmont blues guitarist and barber whose shop in Washington, D.C. served as a hub for blues musicians. He played in the 'East Virginia' style influenced by Blind Boy Fuller and maintained a friendship with Mississippi John Hurt. Edwards was a key figure in keeping the Piedmont tradition alive through the folk revival and beyond.

name: Aron Burton

spentTimePlaces.place: Chicago, South Chicago Township, Cook County, Illinois

description: Aron Burton (June 15, 1938 – February 29, 2016) was an American electric and Chicago blues singer, bass guitarist and songwriter.  In his long career as a sideman with Freddie King, Albert Collins and Junior Wells, he released a number of solo albums, including Good Blues to You (Delmark Records, 1999).  His recorded work was nominated four times for a Blues Music Award in the category Blues Instrumentalist—Bass.

name: Arthur "Big Boy" Crudup

spentTimePlaces.place: Chicago, South Chicago Township, Cook County, Illinois

albums.name: Charly Blues Masterworks Volume 50: Mean Ol' Frisco (1993)
Complete Recorded Works 1941-1956 in Chronological Order, Volume 2: 6 September 1946 to 11 March 1949 (1993)

description: Arthur William "Big Boy" Crudup (August 24, 1905 – March 28, 1974) was an American Delta blues singer, songwriter and guitarist.  He is best known, outside blues circles, for his songs "That's All Right" (1946), "My Baby Left Me" and "So Glad You're Mine", later recorded by Elvis Presley and other artists.

name: Arthur "Big Boy" Spires

spentTimePlaces.place: Chicago, South Chicago Township, Cook County, Illinois

description: Arthur "Big Boy" Spires (February 25, 1912 – October 22, 1990) was an American blues singer and guitarist who recorded for several record labels in Chicago in the 1950s and 1960s.

name: Arthur Crudup
description: Arthur 'Big Boy' Crudup was a Delta blues singer and songwriter who wrote three of Elvis Presley's early hits: 'That's All Right', 'My Baby Left Me', and 'So Glad You're Mine'. Despite his songs' success, Crudup received little compensation and spent much of his life working manual labor jobs. His distinctive guitar style and vocal phrasing influenced the development of rockabilly and rock and roll. Born in Mississippi, he recorded for RCA and other labels in the 1940s and 50s before largely disappearing from music until a late-career revival.

name: Artur Menezes
description: Artur Menezes is a Brazilian blues guitarist who won the Gibson/Albert King Award for Best Guitarist in 2018. He blends fiery blues with jazz grooves and Brazilian rhythms and was selected by Eric Clapton for the Crossroads Guitar Festival.

name: Arvella Gray
description: Arvella Gray, born James Dixon, was a blind blues, folk and gospel singer and guitarist who spent the latter part of his life as a street musician performing at Chicago's Maxwell Street flea market. His only album, The Singing Drifter (1972), showcases his rolling dobro work on traditional gospel numbers and original blues songs.

name: Asie Payton
description:
Asie Reed Payton (April 12, 1937 – May 19, 1997) was an American blues musician, who lived most of his life in Holly Ridge, Mississippi, in the Mississippi Delta.   Born in Washington County, Mississippi, he sang and played the guitar, but made his living as a farmer. 
Near the end of his life he recorded one album, Worried, for the Fat Possum Records label, which was released after his death.

name: Baby Boy Warren

spentTimePlaces.place: Memphis, Shelby County, West Tennessee, Tennessee

description: Baby Boy Warren was a prominent figure in the Detroit blues scene of the 1950s. Originally from Louisiana and raised in Memphis, he absorbed the Delta style from icons like Howlin' Wolf and Little Buddy Doyle. In Detroit, he crafted a sound noted for its witty lyrics and solid guitar work, becoming a staple of the city's blues heritage.

name: Baby Tate
description: Baby Tate (born Bessie Mae Tate, January 28, 1919 – August 21, 1974) was an American Piedmont blues singer and guitarist. She performed and recorded in the 1960s folk blues revival, showcasing traditional country blues style.

name: Barbecue Bob

albums.name: Complete Recorded Works, Volume 2: 21 April 1928 to 3 November 1929 (1991)
Complete Recorded Works, Volume 1: 25 March 1927 to 13 April 1928 (1991)
The Complete Recorded Works, Volume 3: 6 November 1929 to 8 December 1930 (1991)

description: Robert Hicks (September 11, 1902 – October 21, 1931), known as Barbecue Bob, was an American Piedmont blues musician who played 12 string guitar which was popular in the Atlanta, Georgia, area at the time.  A record talent scout gave him his nickname because he worked as a cook in a barbecue restaurant.  One of the two existing photographs of him shows him playing his guitar and wearing a full length, white apron and cook's hat.

name: Barkin' Bill Smith

spentTimePlaces.place: Chicago, South Chicago Township, Cook County, Illinois

description: Barkin' Bill Smith (August 18, 1928 – April 24, 2000) was an American Chicago blues and electric blues singer and songwriter.  He was born in Cleveland, Mississippi, and in his latter years lived in Chicago.

name: Barrelhouse Chuck

spentTimePlaces.place: Chicago, South Chicago Township, Cook County, Illinois

description:
Barrelhouse Chuck (born Harvey Charles Goering; July 10, 1958 – December 12, 2016) was an American Chicago blues and electric blues pianist, keyboardist, singer, and songwriter. 
He claimed to be the only Chicago blues pianist to have studied under Sunnyland Slim, Pinetop Perkins, Blind John Davis, Detroit Junior, and Little Brother Montgomery.   His work appeared on sixteen albums.

name: B.B. King
description: Known as the 'King of the Blues', B.B. King defined the genre with his expressive vibrato and fluid single-note runs on his beloved guitar Lucille. He brought the blues to mainstream audiences worldwide and mentored countless guitarists.

name: Bernice Edwards

spentTimePlaces.place: Chicago, South Chicago Township, Cook County, Illinois

description: Bernice Edwards (c.  1907 – February 26, 1969) was an American classic female blues singer, pianist and songwriter.  She recorded a total of 21 tracks  between 1926 and 1935.

name: Bessie Smith
description: Known as the 'Empress of the Blues', Bessie Smith was the most popular female blues singer of the 1920s and 1930s. Her powerful contralto voice and commanding stage presence made her a dominant force in American music.

name: Bessie Tucker

albums.name: Complete Recorded Works in Chronological Order, 1928-1929 (1991)

description: Bessie Tucker was a powerful Texas blues singer known for her deep voice and songs reflecting the harsh realities of life, particularly prison life. Her 1928 and 1929 recordings, including 'Penitentiary', are considered classics of the genre, though she died young and remains an enigmatic figure.

name: Big Bill Broonzy

spentTimePlaces.place: City of Westminster, Greater London, England, United Kingdom
Chicago, South Chicago Township, Cook County, Illinois
Memphis, Shelby County, West Tennessee, Tennessee

albums.name: A Treasury of Folk Music With Leadbelly (1966)
Hollerin' And Cryin' The Blues, Vol.3 (1980)

description: Big Bill Broonzy (born Lee Conley Bradley; June 26, 1893 or 1903 – August 14, 1958), later known as William Lee Broonzy, was an American blues singer, songwriter, and guitarist.  His career began in the 1920s, when he played country music to mostly African-American audiences.  In the 1930s and 1940s, he navigated a change in style to a more urban blues sound popular with working-class black audiences.

name: Big Boy Henry
description: Richard Leslie Henry  (born May 26, 1921  – December 5, 2004), better known as Big Boy Henry, was an American Piedmont blues guitarist, singer and songwriter.  His most notable recording was  "Mr.  President", a protest against cuts in social welfare undertaken by President Ronald Reagan.

name: Big Jack Johnson
description: Big Jack Johnson (July 30, 1940 – March 14, 2011) was an American electric blues musician from Lambert, Mississippi. A key figure in the Hill Country blues tradition, Johnson was known for his raw, electrified Delta blues sound and his work with the Jelly Roll Kings. He played guitar, mandolin, and vocals, and won a W.C. Handy Award in 2003 for Best Acoustic Blues Album. Johnson was also called 'The Oil Man' due to his work driving trucks for Shell Oil.

name: Big Joe Duskin

spentTimePlaces.place: Chicago, South Chicago Township, Cook County, Illinois

description: Joseph L.  "Big Joe" Duskin (February 10, 1921 – May 6, 2007) was an American blues and boogie-woogie pianist.  He is best known for his debut album, Cincinnati Stomp (1978), and the tracks "Well, Well Baby" and "I Met a Girl Named Martha".

name: Big Joe Turner
description: Big Joe Turner was 'The Boss of the Blues' — a titanic Kansas City blues shouter whose thundering voice could fill any room without a microphone. Born and raised in the jazz-blues hothouse of 1930s Kansas City, his vocal style bridged boogie woogie, jazz, and the emerging rock and roll idiom. His 1954 Atlantic recording 'Shake, Rattle and Roll' became one of the founding documents of rock and roll.

name: Big Joe Williams

spentTimePlaces.place: City of Westminster, Greater London, England, United Kingdom
Chicago, South Chicago Township, Cook County, Illinois
Memphis, Shelby County, West Tennessee, Tennessee

description: Joseph Lee Williams (October 16, 1903 – December 17, 1982) was an American Delta blues guitarist, singer, and songwriter, notable for the distinctive sound of his nine-string guitar.  Performing over five decades, he recorded the songs "Baby, Please Don't Go", "Crawlin' King Snake", and "Peach Orchard Mama", among many others, for various record labels.  He was inducted into the Blues Hall of Fame on October 4, 1992.

name: Big John Wrencher

spentTimePlaces.place: Chicago, South Chicago Township, Cook County, Illinois
Memphis, Shelby County, West Tennessee, Tennessee

description: Big John Wrencher (February 12, 1923 – July 15, 1977), also known as One Arm John, was an American blues harmonica player and singer, well known for playing at the Maxwell Street Market in Chicago in the 1960s.  He toured Europe in the 1970s.

name: Big Maceo Merriweather

spentTimePlaces.place: Chicago, South Chicago Township, Cook County, Illinois

albums.name: The King of Chicago Blues Piano (1992)
The Blues Collection: Big Maceo, Worried Life Blues (1993)
Big Maceo, Volume Two (1945-1950): Big City Blues (2003)

description: Major "Big Maceo" Merriweather (March 31, 1905 – February 23, 1953) was an American pianist and blues singer.  He was mainly active in Chicago through the 1940s.

name: Big Mama Thornton

spentTimePlaces.place: Manhattan, New York County, New York
City of Westminster, Greater London, England, United Kingdom

albums.name: Big Mama Thornton: The Complete Vanguard Recordings (2000)

description:
Willie Mae "Big Mama" Thornton (December 11, 1926 – July 25, 1984), was an American singer and songwriter of blues and R&B. 
The Encyclopedia of Pop, Rock and Soul described Thornton by saying: "Her booming voice, sometimes 200-pound frame, and exuberant stage manner had audiences stomping their feet and shouting encouragement in R&B theaters from coast to coast from the early 1950s on".  Thornton's strong and important vocal style and her confidence on stage made her a huge influence on early blues and rock and roll, even though she rarely received proper credit and compensation for her work.

name: Big Walter Horton

spentTimePlaces.place: Memphis, Shelby County, West Tennessee, Tennessee
Chicago, South Chicago Township, Cook County, Illinois

albums.name: Johnny Shines With Big Walter Horton (1995)

description: Walter Horton (April 6, 1921  – December 8, 1981), known as Big Walter (Horton) or Walter "Shakey" Horton, was an American blues harmonica player.  A quiet, unassuming, shy man, he is remembered as one of the premier harmonica players in the history of blues.  Willie Dixon once called Horton 'the best harmonica player I ever heard'.

name: Bill Jennings
description: Bill Jennings was an American jazz guitarist called "the architect of soul jazz." B.B. King often cited him as a major influence. He recorded with Louis Armstrong, Ella Fitzgerald, and King Curtis.

name: Billy Boy Arnold

albums.name: More Blues On The South Side (Prestige, 1966)

description: William "Billy Boy" Arnold is an American blues harmonica player, singer, and songwriter born in Chicago in 1935. A self-taught musician, he received informal lessons from Sonny Boy Williamson I as a teenager and played harmonica on Bo Diddley's original 1955 recording of "I'm a Man." His original compositions "I Wish You Would" and "I Ain't Got You" were later covered by the Yardbirds and David Bowie. After decades in Chicago blues clubs, he made a celebrated comeback in the 1990s with acclaimed albums on Alligator Records.

name: Billy Branch

albums.name: The Blues Keep Following Me Around (2005)

description: Billy Branch is an American blues harmonica player and bandleader, leading the Sons of Blues since the late 1970s. A protégé of Willie Dixon, he became one of the foremost torchbearers of the Chicago blues harmonica tradition, carrying on the legacy of Little Walter and Big Walter Horton. He has earned multiple Blues Music Award nominations and is a respected educator bringing blues into schools.

name: Billy Wright

albums.name: Blues & Rhythm Series: The Chronological Billy Wright 1949-1951 (2002)

description: Billy Wright (May 21, 1918 – October 28, 1991) was an American R&B and blues singer. A flamboyant performer known as the 'Prince of the Blues,' Wright was a significant influence on Little Richard and recorded for several record labels in the 1940s and 1950s.

name: Black Ace

spentTimePlaces.place: City of Westminster, Greater London, England, United Kingdom

albums.name: I'm the Boss Card in Your Hand (1992)

description: Black Ace (Babe Kyro Lemon Turner) was a Texas blues musician known for playing a National steel guitar flat on his lap. He hosted a radio show in Fort Worth in the late 1930s and recorded his signature song 'Black Ace'. He was rediscovered in 1960 and recorded for Arhoolie Records.

name: Blind Blake

albums.name: Complete Recorded Works in Chronological Order, Volume 2: October 1927 to May 1928 (1991)
Complete Recorded Works in Chronological Order, Volume 1: July 1926 to October 1927 (1991)
Complete Recorded Works in Chronological Order, Volume 4: August 1929 to June 1932 (1991)
Complete Recorded Works in Chronological Order, Volume 3: May 1928 to August 1929 (1991)

description: Arthur Blake (1896 – December 1, 1934), known as Blind Blake, was an American blues and ragtime singer and guitarist.  He is known for recordings he made for Paramount Records between 1926 and 1932.

name: Blind Blues Darby

albums.name: Blind Blues Darby Complete Recorded Works (1935-1937) (Document Records, 1994)

description: Blind Blues Darby (born c. 1900) was an American country blues singer and guitarist active in the 1930s. He recorded several sides for Vocalion Records in 1935-1936, accompanied by guitarist Josh White, showcasing a raw, rural blues style typical of the East Coast Piedmont tradition.

name: Blind Boy Fuller
description: Blind Boy Fuller was the most recorded of the Piedmont blues musicians, known for his ragtime-based fingerpicking guitar style. A prolific recording artist with over 120 songs to his name, he helped popularize the East Coast Piedmont blues style that influenced generations of guitarists including Brownie McGhee and Sonny Terry.

name: Blind John Davis

albums.name: Complete Recorded Works in Chronological Order, Volume 1: 1938-1952 (1999)

description: Blind John Davis (December 7, 1913 – October 12, 1985) was an American blues and boogie-woogie pianist and singer.  He is best remembered for his recordings, including "A Little Every Day" and "Everybody's Boogie".

name: Blind Lemon Jefferson
description: Known as the 'Father of the Texas Blues', Blind Lemon Jefferson was one of the first commercially successful country-blues artists. His high-pitched voice and intricate, fast fingerpicking guitar style influenced generations of blues musicians including Lightnin' Hopkins and T-Bone Walker.

name: Blind Mississippi Morris
description: Blind Mississippi Morris (born Morris Cummings; April 6, 1955 in Clarksdale, Mississippi, United States) is an American blues musician.

name: Blind Willie Johnson

spentTimePlaces.place: Manhattan, New York County, New York

albums.name: Sweeter as the Years Go By (1991)
Dark Was the Night: The Essential Recordings of Blind Willie Johnson (1995)

description: Willie Johnson (January 25, 1897 – September 18, 1945), commonly known as Blind Willie Johnson, was an American gospel blues singer and guitarist.  His landmark recordings completed between 1927 and 1930, thirty songs in all, display a combination of powerful chest voice singing, slide guitar skills and originality that has influenced generations of musicians.  His records sold well though as a street performer and preacher, he had little wealth in his lifetime.

name: Blind Willie McTell

spentTimePlaces.place: Memphis, Shelby County, West Tennessee, Tennessee

description: Blind Willie McTell (born William Samuel McTier; circa 1903 – August 19, 1959) was an American Piedmont blues and ragtime singer, songwriter and guitarist.  He played in a fluid, syncopated finger picking guitar style common among many East Coast, Piedmont blues players.  Like his Atlanta contemporaries, he came to use twelve-string guitars exclusively.

name: Bo Carter
description: Armenter Chatmon, known as Bo Carter, was a member of the influential Mississippi Sheiks and one of the most prolific country blues recording artists of the 1930s, cutting over 110 sides. He is best known for his clever double-entendre songs such as 'Banana in Your Fruit Basket' and 'All Around Man,' and he wrote the original version of the enduring standard 'Corrine, Corrina' in 1928.

name: Bo Diddley

spentTimePlaces.place: Chicago, South Chicago Township, Cook County, Illinois

description: Bo Diddley was a foundational figure in the transition from blues to rock and roll, best known for his syncopated 'Bo Diddley beat' that became one of the most influential rhythmic patterns in popular music. Born in Mississippi and raised in Chicago, he fused blues, R&B, and African rhythms into a wholly original sound that shaped generations of musicians.

name: Bob Corritore
description: Bob Corritore is a highly regarded Chicago-born harmonica player, producer, and radio host. He learned from masters like Big Walter Horton and Carey Bell and has been a prolific figure in recording and producing contemporary and traditional blues albums.

name: Bob Gaddy

spentTimePlaces.place: Manhattan, New York County, New York

description: Bob Gaddy (February 4, 1924 – July 24, 1997) was an American East Coast blues and rhythm-and-blues pianist, singer and songwriter.  He is best remembered for his recordings of "Operator" and "Rip and Run," and musical work he undertook with Larry Dale, Wild Jimmy Spruill, Sonny Terry and Brownie McGhee.

name: Bob Kirkpatrick
description: Bob Kirkpatrick (born January 10, 1934) is an American Texas blues guitarist, singer and songwriter. Known for his classy, jazzy guitar style, he recorded the album 'Going Back to Texas' in 1996 and has worked with many blues musicians in the Texas scene.

name: Bob Margolin

spentTimePlaces.place: City of Westminster, Greater London, England, United Kingdom

description: Bob Margolin (born May 9, 1949) is an American electric blues guitarist.   His nickname is Steady Rollin'.  In 2026 Margolin was inducted into the Blues Hall of Fame.

name: Bob Stroger

albums.name: In the House: Live at Lucerne, Vol. 1 (Crosscut, 2002)

description: Bob Stroger is an American electric blues bass guitarist, singer and songwriter from Hayti, Missouri. After relocating to Chicago in 1955, he became one of the city's most respected and prolific sidemen, backing legends like Otis Rush, Jimmy Rogers, and Sunnyland Slim over a career spanning more than six decades. He has won multiple Blues Music Awards for Instrumentalist - Bass and was inducted into the Blues Hall of Fame in 2025.

name: Bobby 'Blue' Bland
description: Bobby 'Blue' Bland, known as 'The Lion of the Blues,' was one of the most influential blues and soul vocalists of all time. His smooth, gospel-drenched delivery and emotionally raw phrasing defined the Memphis blues sound of the 1950s-60s. Recordings like 'Further on up the Road' and 'I Pity the Fool' on Duke Records made him a permanent fixture in American music history.

name: Bobby Rush

albums.name: Chicken Heads: A 50‐Year History of Bobby Rush (2015)

description: Bobby Rush (born Emmett Ellis Jr., November 23, 1946) is an American blues and R&B musician, singer and songwriter. A veteran of the chitlin' circuit, Rush is known for his energetic stage shows and hits like 'Chicken Heads' and 'Sue'. He has been recording for over 50 years and won a Grammy Award in 2017.

name: Bobo Jenkins

spentTimePlaces.place: City of Westminster, Greater London, England, United Kingdom
Chicago, South Chicago Township, Cook County, Illinois
Memphis, Shelby County, West Tennessee, Tennessee

description: Bobo Jenkins (January 7, 1916 – August 14, 1984) was an American Detroit blues and electric blues guitarist, singer and songwriter.  He also built and set up his own recording studio and record label in Detroit.  Jenkins is best known for his recordings of "Democrat Blues" and "Tell Me Where You Stayed Last Night".

name: Bonnie Raitt

spentTimePlaces.place: Manhattan, New York County, New York
Memphis, Shelby County, West Tennessee, Tennessee

description: Bonnie Lynn Raitt (; born November 8, 1949) is an American singer-songwriter.  In 1971, Raitt released her self-titled debut album.  Following this, she released a series of critically acclaimed roots-influenced albums that incorporated elements of rock, blues, country, and folk.

name: Boo Boo Davis
description: James "Boo Boo" Davis (born November 4, 1943) is an American electric blues musician.  Davis is one of the few remaining blues musicians who gained experience singing the blues in the Mississippi Delta, having sung to help pass the time while picking the cotton fields.

name: Booba Barnes
description: Roosevelt Melvin 'Booba' Barnes (September 25, 1936 – April 2, 1996) was an American Hill Country blues guitarist and vocalist from Longwood, Mississippi. Barnes started his career in 1960 with the Swinging Gold Coasters, later moved to Chicago, then returned to Mississippi in 1971. He opened the Playboy Club nightclub in 1985 and became a regional favorite. His 1990 debut album 'The Heartbroken Man' was hailed as an instant modern classic. Barnes died of lung cancer in 1996.

name: Boogie Bill Webb

spentTimePlaces.place: Chicago, South Chicago Township, Cook County, Illinois

description: Boogie Bill Webb (March 24, 1924 – August 22, 1990) was an American Louisiana blues and rhythm-and-blues guitarist, singer and songwriter.  His music combined Mississippi country blues with New Orleans R&B.  His best-known recordings are "Bad Dog" and "Drinkin' and Stinkin'".

name: Boogie Woogie Red
description: Boogie Woogie Red (October 18, 1925 – July 2, 1992) was an American Detroit blues, boogie-woogie and jazz pianist, singer and songwriter.  At different times he worked with Sonny Boy Williamson I, Washboard Willie, Baby Boy Warren, Lonnie Johnson, Tampa Red, John Lee Hooker and Memphis Slim.

name: Boyd Gilmore

spentTimePlaces.place: Memphis, Shelby County, West Tennessee, Tennessee

description: Boyd Gilmore (June 1, 1905 or June 12, 1910 – December 23, 1976) was an American Delta blues singer, guitarist and songwriter.  Among the songs he wrote were "All in My Dreams", "Believe I'll Settle Down", "I Love My Little Woman" and "If That's Your Girl".  Gilmore also recorded a version of fellow Delta bluesman Robert Johnson's track, "Ramblin' on My Mind".

description: Buddy Guy bridged the Chicago blues tradition with the coming rock era. His wild, feedback-drenched guitar style directly influenced Jimi Hendrix, Eric Clapton, and Stevie Ray Vaughan, who all cited him as a primary inspiration.

description: Tiny Grimes was a jazz and R&B guitarist notable for his electric four-string tenor guitar. He co-headlined the first Moondog Coronation Ball in 1952, considered the first rock and roll concert.

name: Titus Turner

albums.name: Blues & Rhythm Series: The Chronological Titus Turner 1949-1954 (2005)

description: Titus Lee Turner (May 1, 1933 – September 13, 1984) was an American R&B and East Coast blues singer and songwriter.  His best-remembered recordings are "We Told You Not to Marry" and "Sound-Off".  He also wrote "Leave My Kitten Alone", "Sticks and Stones" and "Tell Me Why".

name: Tom Delaney
description: Tom Delaney (c. 1889 – c. 1963) was an American classic female blues songwriter and singer. He wrote several popular blues songs in the 1920s including 'Down Home Blues' and 'Terrible Blues', which were recorded by Bessie Smith and other blues singers of the era.

name: Tommy Johnson
description: Tommy Johnson was an influential Delta blues musician whose distinctive falsetto and slide guitar style inspired the 'devil at the crossroads' myth, later misattributed to Robert Johnson. His recordings for Victor in 1928, including 'Canned Heat Blues' and 'Maggie Campbell Blues', became classics of the Delta blues genre. Unlike many bluesmen of his era, Johnson had a relatively light repertoire but each song was masterfully crafted. His music influenced later generations of blues and rock musicians.

name: Tracy Nelson
description: Tracy Nelson is a country and blues singer who fronted Mother Earth in the late 1960s San Francisco scene. Her signature song "Down So Low" has been covered by Linda Ronstadt and Etta James.

name: Turner Foddrell

albums.name: The Foddrell Brothers: Carolina Blues Breeze (1983)

description: Turner Foddrell (June 22, 1928 – January 31, 1995) was an American Piedmont blues and folk acoustic guitarist, singer and songwriter.  He performed locally, nationally, and in Europe, both as a solo artist and with his brother, Marvin.  They jointly recorded two albums in the early 1980s.

name: Tutu Jones
description: Tutu Jones (born September 9, 1966) is an American electric blues and soul blues guitarist, singer and songwriter.  He has cited Freddie King and Z.  Z.

name: Tyler Bryant

spentTimePlaces.place: Nashville, Davidson County, Middle Tennessee, Tennessee

description: Tyler Bryant is a Texas-born guitar prodigy who relocated to Nashville to form Tyler Bryant & The Shakedown. Strongly influenced by Muddy Waters, his playing incorporates southern Americana grooves and high-energy blues rock.

description: Huary Perry "U. P. " Wilson (September 4, 1934 – September 22, 2004) was an American electric blues guitarist and singer who performed Texas blues.

name: Valerie Wellington
description: Valerie Wellington (November 14, 1959 – January 2, 1993) was an American singer who, in her short career, switched from singing opera to singing Chicago blues and electric blues.  On her 1984 album, Million Dollar Secret, she worked with Sunnyland Slim, Billy Branch, and Magic Slim.  She also worked with Lee "Shot" Williams.

name: Van Morrison

spentTimePlaces.place: City of Westminster, Greater London, England, United Kingdom

description: Van Morrison is a Northern Irish singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist whose music weaves blues, jazz, folk, and soul into a deeply personal style. His gritty vocal delivery and harmonica playing are rooted in the blues tradition, and albums like 'Too Long in Exile' — recorded with John Lee Hooker — showcase his lifelong devotion to the genre.

name: Vanessa Collier

albums.name: Do It My Own Way (Phenix Fire, 2024)

description: Vanessa Collier is an American blues, funk, and soul saxophonist, singer and songwriter born in Dallas, Texas and raised in Columbia, Maryland. After graduating from Berklee College of Music, she toured backing Joe Louis Walker before launching her solo career. She has won multiple Blues Music Awards for Instrumentalist - Horn and Contemporary Blues Female Artist, and is a Selmer-endorsed woodwind artist.

name: Victoria Spivey

albums.name: Complete Recorded Works In Chronological Order Volume 4 (30 August 1936-21 July 1937) (1995)

description: Victoria Regina Spivey (October 15, 1906 – October 3, 1976), sometimes known as Queen Victoria, was an American blues singer, songwriter, and record company founder.  During a recording career that spanned 40 years, from 1926 to the mid-1960s, she worked with  Louis Armstrong, King Oliver, Clarence Williams, Luis Russell, Lonnie Johnson, and Bob Dylan.  She also performed in vaudeville and clubs, sometimes with her sisters Addie "Sweet Peas" (or "Sweet Pease") Spivey and Elton Island Spivey (also known as the Za Zu Girl).

name: Virginia Liston

spentTimePlaces.place: Manhattan, New York County, New York

albums.name: Complete Recorded Works In Chronological Order Volume 1 (1923-1924) (1996)

description: Virginia Liston (née Crawford; c.  1890 – June 1932) was an American classic female blues and jazz singer.  She spent most of her career in vaudeville.

name: W.C. Handy
description: William Christopher Handy, known as the 'Father of the Blues,' was an American composer, musician, and bandleader who was one of the first to publish music in the blues form. His compositions including 'St. Louis Blues,' 'Memphis Blues,' and 'Beale Street Blues' helped transform the blues from a regional Delta music style into a nationally popular genre, taking it to a new level of popularity.

name: Walter Brown

albums.name: Blues & Rhythm Series: The Chronological Walter Brown 1945-1947 (2001)
Blues & Rhythm Series: The Chronological Walter Brown 1947-1951 (2002)

description: Walter Brown (August 31, 1919 – May 25, 1956) was an American R&B and blues singer. He recorded with Jay McShann's orchestra and had hits with 'Don't You Want a Man Like Me' and 'Confessin' the Blues'.

name: Walter Roland

spentTimePlaces.place: Manhattan, New York County, New York

Complete Recorded Works in Chronological Order, Volume 1: 1933

description: Walter Roland (possibly December 20, 1902 – October 12, 1972) was an American blues and boogie-woogie pianist, guitarist and singer, noted for his association with Lucille Bogan, Josh White and Sonny Scott.  The music journalist Gérard Herzhaft stated that Roland was "a great piano player...  as comfortable in boogie-woogies as in slow blues," adding that "Roland – with his manner of playing and his singing – was direct and rural.

name: Walter Vinson

description: Walter Vinson (February 2, 1901 – April 22, 1975) was an American Memphis blues guitarist, singer and songwriter.  He was a member of the Mississippi Sheiks, worked with Bo Chatmon and his brothers, and co-wrote the blues standard "Sitting on Top of the World".  He is erroneously known as Walter Vincson or Walter Vincent.

name: Walter "Wolfman" Washington
description: Walter 'Wolfman' Washington was a New Orleans guitarist and singer who blended blues, funk, and R&B into his own distinctive sound. He began his career as a teenager in Lee Dorsey's band, later spending twenty years alongside Johnny Adams before forming his own group, the Roadmasters. A beloved fixture at clubs like the Maple Leaf Bar and d.b.a, his guitar style drew deeply from the New Orleans traditions of Guitar Slim and Professor Longhair.

description: Robert Clifford Brown (July 15, 1910 – November 6, 1966), known professionally as Washboard Sam, was an American blues musician and singer.

name: Washboard Willie
description: William Paden Hensley (July 24, 1906 or 1909 – August 24, 1991), known as Washboard Willie, was an American Detroit blues musician, who specialised in playing the washboard.  He recorded tracks including "A Fool on a Mule in the Middle of The Road" plus "Cherry Red Blues", and worked variously with Eddie "Guitar" Burns, Baby Boy Warren, and Boogie Woogie Red.

name: Whistlin' Alex Moore

albums.name: Complete Recorded Works 1929-1951 In Chronological Order (1993)
From North Dallas To The East Side (1994)

description: Alexander Herman "Whistlin' Alex" Moore (November 22, 1899 – January 20, 1989), was an American blues pianist, singer and whistler.  He is best remembered for his recordings of "Blue Bloomer Blues" (which he first recorded in 1929, as well as later in life), "Across the Atlantic Ocean" and "Black Eyed Peas and Hog Jowls".

name: William Clarke
description: William Clarke (July 21, 1951 – November 2, 1996) was an American blues harmonica player. A leading figure in the West Coast blues scene, Clarke was known for his powerful amplified harmonica playing and his work with the Hollywood Fats Band and as a solo artist.

name: Willie 61 Blackwell
description: Willie "61" Blackwell was a country blues guitarist who took his nickname from Route 61. He was recorded by Alan Lomax in 1942 and was reportedly taught guitar by Robert Johnson.

name: Willie Brown

albums.name: Son House and the Great Delta Blues Singers (1928-1930) (1990)

description: Willie Lee Brown (1899 or August 6, 1900 – December 30, 1952) was an American blues guitar player and vocalist.  He performed and recorded with other blues musicians, including Son House and Charlie Patton, and influenced Robert Johnson and Muddy Waters.  Brown is considered one of the pioneering musicians of the Delta blues genre.

name: Willie Cobbs

Memphis, Shelby County, West Tennessee, Tennessee

description: Willie C.  Cobbs (July 15, 1932 – October 25, 2021) was an American blues singer, harmonica player and songwriter.  He is best known for his song "You Don't Love Me".

name: Willie D. Warren

spentTimePlaces.place: Chicago, South Chicago Township, Cook County, Illinois

description: Willie D.  Warren (September 11, 1924 – December 30, 2000) was an American electric blues guitarist, bass player and singer.  In a long career, he worked with Otis Rush, Al Benson, Little Sonny Cooper, David Honeyboy Edwards, Baby Boy Warren, Guitar Slim, Freddie King, Jimmy Reed, Morris Pejoe, Bobo Jenkins and Jim McCarty.

name: Willie Dixon

spentTimePlaces.place: Manhattan, New York County, New York
Chicago, South Chicago Township, Cook County, Illinois
Memphis, Shelby County, West Tennessee, Tennessee
