description: William James Dixon (July 1, 1915 – January 29, 1992) was an American blues musician, vocalist, songwriter, arranger and record producer.  He was proficient in playing both the upright bass and the guitar, and sang with a distinctive voice, but he is perhaps best known as one of the most prolific songwriters of his time.  Next to Muddy Waters, Dixon is recognized as the most influential person in shaping the post–World War II sound of the Chicago blues.

name: Willie Love
description: Willie Love Jr.  (November 4, 1906 – August 19, 1953) was an American Delta blues pianist.  He is best known for his association with and accompaniment of Sonny Boy Williamson II.

name: Willie Mabon

albums.name: Willie Mabon Sings 'I Don't Know' and Other Chicago Blues Hits (1976)

description: Willie Mabon (October 24, 1925 - April 19, 1985) was an American R&B singer, songwriter, pianist and harmonica player who scored two number-one Billboard R&B hits with 'I Don't Know' in 1952 and 'I'm Mad' in 1953. A key Chess Records artist, he was the first to record Willie Dixon's 'The Seventh Son.' He relocated to Paris in 1972 and toured extensively in Europe before his death.

name: Willie Trice
description: William Augusta Trice (February 10, 1908 – December 11, 1976) was an American blues guitarist, singer and songwriter.  He released two singles and an album.  He remained loyal to his native North Carolina and its regional blues style, often referred to as Piedmont blues, East Coast blues, or more generally country blues.

name: Woodrow Adams

spentTimePlaces.place: Memphis, Shelby County, West Tennessee, Tennessee

description: Woodrow Wilson Adams (April 9, 1917 – August 9, 1988) was an American Delta blues guitarist and harmonica player.  He made a late entry into the recording industry, producing three singles.  His most accomplished song was "How Long", which offered an insight into his lifestyle.

name: Woody Guthrie
description: Woody Guthrie was a folk musician known as the "Dust Bowl Troubadour" for songs like "This Land Is Your Land." His 1940 album Dust Bowl Ballads influenced Bob Dylan, Johnny Cash, and Bruce Springsteen.

name: Wynonie Harris

spentTimePlaces.place: Los Angeles, Los Angeles County, California

albums.name: Bloodshot Eyes: The Best of Wynonie Harris (1994)

description: Wynonie Harris (August 24, 1915 – June 14, 1969) was an American blues shouter best remembered as a singer of upbeat songs, featuring humorous, often ribald lyrics.  He had fifteen Top 10 hits between 1946 and 1952.  Harris is attributed by many music scholars to be one of the founding fathers of rock and roll.

name: Yank Rachell

albums.name: Too Hot for the Devil (Blue Goose, 1997)

description: Yank Rachell was an American country blues musician and a master of the blues mandolin whose performing career spanned nearly seventy years, from the late 1920s to the 1990s. He frequently collaborated with Sleepy John Estes and wrote "She Caught the Katy," which became a blues standard. Often called an "elder statesman of the blues," he was one of the last active musicians whose career began in the 1920s.

name: Z. Z. Hill

albums.name: Greatest Hits: Dues Paid In Full (1971)
The Complete Hill Records Collection / UA Recordings. 1972 - 1975 (1996)
That's It! The Complete Kent Recordings 1964-1968 (2018)

description: Z. Z. Hill (September 30, 1935 – April 27, 1984) was an American soul blues singer and songwriter. Known as 'The Ruby of the Soul Blues,' Hill recorded for Kent, Minit, and Hill labels, and scored several R&B hits including 'Cheatin' in the Next Room' and 'Down Home Blues.' His emotionally powerful voice and storytelling ability made him a favorite among Southern soul blues fans.

name: Zora Young
description:
Zora Young (born January 21, 1948, West Point, Mississippi, United States) is an American blues singer.  She is distantly related to Howlin' Wolf. 
Young's family moved to Chicago when she was seven.

name: Z.Z. Hill
description: Z.Z. Hill was a popular blues and soul singer who successfully blended traditional blues with Southern soul. Starting in the 1950s recording for various labels, he found his greatest success with Malaco Records in Jackson, Mississippi. His 1982 album 'Down Home' became a landmark of modern blues, featuring his biggest hit 'Down Home Blues'. Hill's smooth yet powerful voice conveyed both deep emotion and jukejoint energy, making him one of the most successful blues artists of the 1980s.

name: Sister Rosetta Tharpe
description: Sister Rosetta Tharpe was an American singer, songwriter, and guitarist who gained popularity in the 1930s and 1940s with her gospel recordings, characterized by a unique mixture of spiritual lyrics and electric guitar. She was the first great recording star of gospel music and was among the first gospel musicians to appeal to rhythm and blues and rock and roll audiences, later being referred to as 'the original soul sister' and 'the Godmother of rock and roll'. Her guitar-playing technique had a profound influence on the development of British blues in the 1960s.

name: Marie Knight
description: Marie Knight was an American gospel and rhythm and blues singer. She was discovered by Sister Rosetta Tharpe in 1946 and the two toured and recorded together through the late 1940s, scoring hits like 'Up Above My Head' which reached number six on the US R&B chart. After going solo in the 1950s, Knight recorded both gospel and secular R&B for labels including Decca, Mercury, and Okeh, and continued performing until her death in 2009.

name: Mahalia Jackson

albums.name: Great Songs of Love and Faith (1962)

description: Mahalia Jackson was an American gospel singer, widely considered one of the most influential vocalists of the 20th century. With a career spanning 40 years, she was integral to the development and spread of gospel blues in black churches throughout the U.S., selling an estimated 22 million records and performing for integrated and secular audiences in concert halls around the world. Completely self-taught, she was renowned for her powerful contralto voice and enormous stage presence, and is credited with inspiring rhythm and blues, soul, and rock and roll singing styles.

name: Mavis Staples

albums.name: If All I Was Was Black (2017)

description: Mavis Staples is an American rhythm and blues and gospel singer and civil rights activist. She rose to fame as a member of her family's band the Staple Singers, of which she is the last surviving member, recording the hit singles 'I'll Take You There' and 'Let's Do It Again'. A Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award recipient and Rock and Roll Hall of Fame inductee, she has collaborated with artists including Bob Dylan, Prince, Ry Cooder, and Jeff Tweedy across a solo career spanning over five decades.

name: Aretha Franklin

albums.name: I Never Loved a Man the Way I Love You (1967)

description: Aretha Louise Franklin was an American singer, songwriter and pianist. Regarded as the 'Queen of Soul', she was twice named by Rolling Stone magazine as the greatest singer of all time. She recorded landmark albums such as I Never Loved a Man the Way I Love You, Lady Soul, and Amazing Grace, and became one of the best-selling music artists with more than 75 million records sold worldwide.

name: Nina Simone

albums.name: I Put a Spell on You (1965)

description: Nina Simone was an American pianist, singer, songwriter, and civil rights activist. Her music spanned styles including classical, folk, gospel, blues, jazz, R&B, and pop. Her piano playing was strongly influenced by baroque and classical music, especially Johann Sebastian Bach, and accompanied expressive, jazz-like singing in her contralto voice.

name: Billie Holiday
description: Billie Holiday was an American jazz and swing music singer, nicknamed 'Lady Day' by her friend and music partner Lester Young. She made significant contributions to jazz music and pop singing, with a vocal style strongly influenced by jazz instrumentalists that inspired a new way of manipulating phrasing and tempo. Holiday was known for her vocal delivery and improvisational skills, and was ranked fourth on Rolling Stone's list of the 200 Greatest Singers of All Time.

name: Ella Fitzgerald

albums.name: Ella Fitzgerald Sings the Cole Porter Song Book (1956)
Ella in Berlin: Mack the Knife (1960)

description: Ella Jane Fitzgerald was an American singer, songwriter and composer, sometimes referred to as the 'First Lady of Song', 'Queen of Jazz', and 'Lady Ella'. She was noted for her purity of tone, impeccable diction, phrasing, timing, intonation, and a 'horn-like' improvisational ability, particularly in her scat singing. After a tumultuous adolescence, Fitzgerald found stability in musical success with the Chick Webb Orchestra, performing across the country but most often associated with the Savoy Ballroom in Harlem.

name: T-Model Ford
description: James Lewis Carter Ford, known as T-Model Ford, was an American blues musician who began his musical career in his early seventies. He continuously recorded for the Fat Possum record label before eventually moving to Alive Naturalsound Records. His musical style combined the rawness of Delta blues with Chicago and juke joint blues styles.

name: Bernard Allison
description: Bernard Allison is an American blues guitarist and singer, based in Paris, France. The son of Chicago blues musician Luther Allison, he taught himself guitar in Florida while listening to his father's records and joined Koko Taylor's touring band at age 18. Allison became bandleader for his father's European touring band in 1989 and has since released over twenty albums, with his 2002 album Storms of Life reaching number five on the Billboard Top Blues Albums chart.

name: Sam Lay
description: Sam Lay was an American blues drummer and vocalist who performed alongside Little Walter, Howlin' Wolf, Muddy Waters, and Bob Dylan. He was the drummer when Dylan went electric at the 1965 Newport Folk Festival and recorded on Highway 61 Revisited. A founding member of the Paul Butterfield Blues Band, he was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2015 and the Blues Hall of Fame in the late 1980s.

name: Sam Carr
description: Sam Carr was an American blues drummer best known as a member of the Jelly Roll Kings. The son of blues musician Robert Nighthawk, he contributed his distinctive minimalist drumming to albums by numerous Delta blues artists including Sonny Boy Williamson II, David Honeyboy Edwards, and Buddy Guy.

name: Willie "Big Eyes" Smith
description: Willie "Big Eyes" Smith was an American electric blues drummer best known for his long association with Muddy Waters' band from 1961 to 1980. He co-founded The Legendary Blues Band and won a Grammy Award for Best Traditional Blues Album in 2011 for "Joined at the Hip" with Pinetop Perkins.

name: Tony Coleman
description: Tony Coleman is a legendary blues drummer best known as the backbone of B.B. King's band for 29 years. Born in Kissimmee, Florida, he has backed countless soul and blues legends including Bobby "Blue" Bland, Albert King, and Etta James, touring 98 countries worldwide.

name: Nathan East
description: Nathan East is an American jazz, R&B, and rock bass guitarist and vocalist. With more than 2,000 recordings, he is one of the most recorded bass players in the history of music. He is a founding member of contemporary jazz quartet Fourplay and has performed with Eric Clapton, Phil Collins, Stevie Wonder, and Daft Punk.

name: Jason Ricci
description: Jason Ricci is an American harmonica player and singer known for his virtuosic technique and innovative overblowing style. He was named Best Harmonica Player at the 2010 Blues Music Awards and performed on Johnny Winter's Grammy-winning 2014 album Step Back.

name: Walter Trout
description: Walter Trout is an American blues rock guitarist and singer whose career spans five decades. He served as lead guitarist for John Mayall's Bluesbreakers and Canned Heat before launching a prolific solo career with over twenty albums. He survived a life-threatening liver failure in 2014 and returned to recording and touring.

name: Johnnie Johnson
description: Johnnie Clyde Johnson was an American pianist who played jazz, blues, and rock and roll. His work with Chuck Berry led to his induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, and he was the leader of Albert King's rhythm section during King's most prolific period. He was a cornerstone of the St. Louis blues scene.

name: Mitch Woods
description: Mitch Woods is an American boogie-woogie, jump blues, and jazz pianist and singer. Since the early 1980s he has been touring with his band the Rocket 88s, carrying on the tradition of 1940s and 1950s jump blues and boogie-woogie piano.

name: Sugar Pie DeSanto

albums.name: Down In The Basement: The Chess Years (1989)

description: Sugar Pie DeSanto was an American R&B singer and dancer whose career flourished in the 1950s and 1960s. Discovered by Johnny Otis in 1955, she signed with Chess Records and scored hits including 'I Want to Know' and the Etta James duets 'Do I Make Myself Clear' and 'In the Basement'. A 2024 Blues Hall of Fame inductee, she was renowned for her electrifying stage performances.

name: James Booker
description: James Carroll Booker III was an American New Orleans rhythm and blues keyboardist of extraordinary technical skill, dubbed 'the Black Liberace.' His 1960 recording 'Gonzo' reached No. 3 on the R&B chart, and he profoundly influenced the New Orleans music scene, fusing rhythm and blues with jazz in his signature backbeat style.

name: Jonny Lang
description: Jonny Lang is an American blues, gospel, and rock singer, songwriter, and guitarist from Fargo, North Dakota. He had a major hit at age 15 with 'Lie to Me' and has recorded five albums that charted on the Billboard 200. He won a Grammy Award for his 2006 album Turn Around.

name: Frank Frost
description: Frank Frost was one of the foremost American Delta blues harmonica players of his generation. He toured with Sonny Boy Williamson II, who taught him harmonica, and later formed The Jelly Roll Kings with Sam Carr, becoming a staple of the Arkansas blues scene.

name: De Ford Bailey
description: DeFord Bailey was the first African American country music star and a pioneering harmonica wizard who helped establish the Grand Ole Opry. He developed his unique train-imitation style while recovering from childhood polio, creating sounds that mimicked the locomotives and countryside wildlife around his Tennessee home. Bailey was the first performer to record in Nashville and influenced generations of harmonica players before his career was cut short by a royalties dispute in 1941.

name: Watermelon Slim
description: William P. Homans III, known professionally as Watermelon Slim, is an American blues musician renowned for playing slide guitar lap-style, left-handed and backwards, using a Zippo lighter as a slide. A Vietnam veteran turned truck driver and farmer, he launched his music career with the anti-war album Merry Airbrakes in 1973 and went on to win multiple Blues Music Awards including Best Blues Band and Best Blues Album in 2008.

name: Johnny Nicholas
description: Johnny Nicholas is an American blues musician from Westerly, Rhode Island, best known as a multi-instrumentalist who plays guitar, piano, harmonica, and mandolin. He gained prominence as a member of the Grammy Award-winning western swing group Asleep at the Wheel and has recorded with blues legends including Big Walter Horton, Robert Lockwood Jr., and Johnny Shines. Since 1981, he has owned and operated the Hill Top Cafe near Fredericksburg, Texas while continuing to perform and record.

name: Jed Davenport
description: Jed Davenport was a Mississippi-born blues harmonica player who settled in Memphis and led the Beale Street Jug Band in the late 1920s. He also played guitar, trumpet, and jug, performing regularly on Beale Street when not touring with medicine shows. His recorded output consists of sessions from 1929-1930 for Victor Records, featuring his distinctive harmonica work in the Memphis jug band tradition.

name: Garfield Akers
description: Garfield Akers was an American blues singer and guitarist from Hernando, Mississippi, who recorded only four sides in 1929–1930, most notably the two-part 'Cottonfield Blues' with Mississippi Joe Callicott. His driving guitar rhythms and piercing vocal style have been hailed as an early precursor to rock and roll.

name: Cecil Augusta
description: Cecil Augusta was an American Delta blues singer and guitarist who recorded two tracks for Alan Lomax in Memphis, Tennessee, in 1959, including 'Stop All the Buses'. Musicologist David Evans described him as a unique acoustic guitarist whose technique anticipated electric blues playing.

name: Nathan Beauregard
description: Nathan Beauregard was a blind American blues singer and guitarist from Benton County, Mississippi. Born blind, he became a musician with a repertoire of pre-blues era songs and dance tunes but was never offered a recording deal during the 1920s race recordings era. Rediscovered in 1968 during the folk and blues revival, he spent his final years performing at festivals and recording on labels including Blue Horizon, Blue Thumb, Arhoolie, and Adelphi.

name: Jimmy Bertrand
description: Jimmy Bertrand was an American jazz and blues percussionist born in Biloxi, Mississippi, who was active on the Chicago blues and jazz scene of the 1920s. He recorded with numerous artists and led Jimmy Bertrand's Washboard Wizards, and was also a noted instructor whose pupils included Lionel Hampton.

name: Dennis Binder
description: Dennis Binder is an American rhythm and blues musician and singer-songwriter born in Rosedale, Mississippi, best known for his song 'Long Man Blues'. He began his career in the 1950s recording for prominent labels including Chess, Sun, and Modern Records, and collaborated with Ike Turner's Kings of Rhythm.

name: Mr. Bo
description: Louis Collins, known professionally as Mr. Bo, was an American electric blues guitarist, singer and songwriter born in Indianola, Mississippi. Primarily working as a live performer in Detroit for four decades, his co-written song 'If Trouble Was Money' was later recorded by both Charlie Musselwhite and Albert Collins.

name: Houston Boines

albums.name: Sun: The Roots Of Rock: Volume 2 - Sam's Blues (1976)
The Modern Downhome Blues Sessions, Volume 2 (2003)

description: Houston Boines was an American blues harmonica player and singer from Hazlehurst, Mississippi. Recruited by talent scout Ike Turner, he recorded for Modern Records in 1952 and for Sun Records in 1953. He also broadcast on the legendary King Biscuit Time radio program on KFFA in Helena, Arkansas.

name: Charley Booker
description: Charley Booker was an American blues singer and guitarist from the Mississippi Delta who recorded in the early 1950s for Modern Records. He learned guitar from his uncle, who had played with Charley Patton, and worked with notable musicians including Ike Turner and Elmore James in the Greenville, Mississippi area.

name: R. L. Boyce
description: R. L. Boyce was an American blues singer, songwriter, and guitarist born and raised in Como, Mississippi. A protege of Hill Country blues legends R. L. Burnside and Mississippi Fred McDowell, he began his career playing drums before becoming a Grammy-nominated solo artist. His 2017 album Roll and Tumble was nominated for a Grammy Award, and in 2023 he received a National Heritage Fellowship from the NEA.

name: Jackie Brenston
description: Jackie Brenston was an American singer and saxophonist who, with Ike Turner's band the Kings of Rhythm, recorded 'Rocket 88' in 1951 at Sam Phillips' studio in Memphis. The song reached number one on the Billboard R&B chart and is widely considered one of the first rock and roll records.

name: Eden Brent
description: Eden Brent is an American blues pianist and vocalist from Greenville, Mississippi who combines boogie-woogie with elements of blues, jazz, soul, gospel and pop. A protege of Abie 'Boogaloo' Ames, she earned the nickname 'Little Boogaloo' and won the Blues Foundation's International Blues Challenge in 2006.

name: Jim Brewer
description: Jim Brewer was an American blues singer and guitarist born in Brookhaven, Mississippi. He moved to Chicago in the 1940s and became a fixture on Maxwell Street, busking and performing both blues and gospel songs. During the 1960s blues revival, he recorded for Heritage, Flyright, and Testament Records.

name: Big George Brock
description: Big George Brock was an American blues harmonica player and singer born in Grenada, Mississippi, who moved to St. Louis in 1950 and became a central figure in the city's blues scene. He operated the legendary Club Caravan nightclub where he hosted Muddy Waters, Howlin' Wolf, and Ike and Tina Turner.

name: J. T. Brown

albums.name: Blues Jam in Chicago Vol. 1 with Fleetwood Mac (1969)

description: J. T. Brown was an American tenor saxophonist of the Chicago blues era, known for his distinctive braying tone. Born in Mississippi, he became a prolific session musician in Chicago, recording with Elmore James, Howlin' Wolf, and notably appearing on Fleetwood Mac's 1969 Blues Jam in Chicago sessions.

name: Kenny Brown
description: Kenny Brown is an American blues slide guitarist born in Selma, Alabama, and raised in Nesbit, Mississippi, where he apprenticed with Mississippi Joe Callicott from age twelve. He spent over two decades as R.L. Burnside's guitarist and protege, becoming a key figure in the North Mississippi Hill Country blues tradition.

name: Texas Johnny Brown
description: Texas Johnny Brown was an American blues guitarist, songwriter and singer best known for composing 'Two Steps from the Blues', which became the title track of Bobby Bland's 1961 album. Born in Ackerman, Mississippi, he relocated to Houston, Texas in 1946 where his jazzy guitar style made him a mainstay of the city's blues scene for over six decades.

name: Eddie Burks
description: Eddie Burks was an American blues harmonica player and singer born near Greenwood, Mississippi, who became a fixture on Chicago's Maxwell Street Market in the 1960s and 1970s, earning the nickname 'Jewtown Eddie'. After years as a steel mill worker and storefront church minister, he launched a full-time blues career following the 1968 assassination of Martin Luther King Jr.

name: Charles Caldwell
description: Charles Caldwell was an American musician from the North Mississippi hill country known for a raw and fiery brand of electric blues. A lifelong resident of Coffeeville, Mississippi, his sole album, Remember Me, was recorded for Fat Possum Records shortly before his death from pancreatic cancer in 2003 and released posthumously to critical acclaim.

name: Eddie C. Campbell
description: Eddie C. Campbell was an American Chicago blues guitarist and singer who moved to Chicago at age ten and learned directly from Muddy Waters, Magic Sam, and Otis Rush. He played as a sideman with Howlin' Wolf, Little Walter, and Jimmy Reed before joining Willie Dixon's Chicago Blues All-Stars in 1976.

name: Grady Champion
description: Grady Champion is an American electric blues harmonicist, singer, guitarist and songwriter born in Canton, Mississippi. He blends authentic Mississippi juke joint blues with modern soul and R&B, winning a Grammy Award in 2003 for co-writing 'Trust Yourself' on Etta James' album Let's Roll. He won the 26th International Blues Challenge in 2010.

name: Willie Clayton
description: Willie Clayton is an American soul-blues singer and songwriter born in Indianola, Mississippi, who relocated to Chicago in 1971 and became a prominent figure in Chicago blues alongside Buddy Guy, Koko Taylor, and Little Milton. He has recorded over 25 albums since the 1980s with multiple chart successes on the Billboard Top Blues Albums and R&B charts.

name: Lee Cooper
description: Lee Cooper was an American blues guitarist from Lexington, Mississippi, who succeeded Willie Johnson as Howlin' Wolf's lead guitarist and played on many of Wolf's most successful Chess Records sessions. Eddie Boyd called him 'the best guitar I ever played with,' and his aggressive licks anticipated those of Chuck Berry by several years.

name: George Cummings

albums.name: The Final Years: Big Joe Williams (1993)

description: George Cummings was an American guitarist and songwriter born in Meridian, Mississippi, best known as the founder and naming member of Dr. Hook & the Medicine Show. He collaborated with Delta bluesman Big Joe Williams at Muscle Shoals in 1978 on one of Williams' final recordings.

name: Eddie Cusic
description: Eddie Cusic was an American Mississippi Delta blues guitarist, singer, and songwriter born in Wilmot, Mississippi. In the early 1950s he formed the Rhythm Aces, a band that included Little Milton, whom Cusic taught to play guitar. His debut album was released in 1998 and hailed as a significant blues discovery.

name: Lester Davenport
description: Lester Davenport was a Chicago blues harmonica player and singer who moved from Mississippi to Chicago at age 14. He backed Bo Diddley on a 1955 Chess Records session and played with Snooky Pryor, Homesick James, and others before releasing his debut album at age 60.

name: James Lee Davis III
description: Jamie Davis is a Mississippi-born country, soul, and blues rock musician best known as the lead singer and guitarist of Jamie Davis & Soul Gravy. The band's 2006 single "Mississippi Moonshine" brought them regional recognition throughout the South. Davis later gained wider fame as a Nashville songwriter, co-writing Luke Combs' hit "The Kind of Love We Make."

name: Little Sammy Davis
description: Little Sammy Davis was a blues harmonica player and singer born in Winona, Mississippi, who toured extensively with Earl Hooker and performed alongside Muddy Waters, Jimmy Reed, and Little Walter during the Chicago blues era. After a two-decade absence from music, he was rediscovered in the 1990s and launched a celebrated comeback, becoming a regular on the Imus in the Morning radio show and later joining Levon Helm's band for the Midnight Ramble concerts.

albums.name: The Midnight Ramble Sessions Volume One

name: Mattie Delaney
description: Mattie Delaney was an American Delta blues singer and guitarist active in the late 1920s and 1930s, known for recording only two songs for Vocalion Records in February 1930. She was unusual for a female performer of her era in that she accompanied herself on guitar and sang topical songs. Her recorded output, "Down the Big Road Blues" and "Tallahatchie River Blues," showcases a raw, country blues style deeply rooted in the Mississippi Delta tradition.

name: Johnny Drummer
description: Johnny Drummer (born Thessex Johns) is a Chicago blues and soul blues multi-instrumentalist from Alligator, Mississippi, who moved to Chicago in 1959. He became a fixture on the city's blues scene, playing drums for Eddie King and sitting in with legends like Muddy Waters and Big Walter Horton before forming his own band, the Starliters.

name: Calep H. Emphrey Jr.
description: Calep H. Emphrey Jr. was a blues drummer best known as the drummer for B.B. King's band for over 30 years, from 1977 to 2009. Born in Greenville, Mississippi, he began his career with Little Milton's band before playing with Freddie King and Albert King, earning a reputation as a master of the left-handed shuffle.

name: Willie Cris Farmer
description: Little Willie Farmer is a Mississippi Hill Country blues guitarist, singer, and songwriter who spent three decades running an auto repair shop in Duck Hill while performing on evenings and weekends. Discovered via YouTube in 2016, he has released two critically acclaimed albums and was described by DownBeat as one of the real finds in recent memory.

name: Baby Face Leroy Foster
description: Baby Face Leroy Foster was an American blues singer, guitarist and drummer who played a significant role in the development of the postwar electric Chicago blues sound as a member of Muddy Waters early band. His 1950 Parkway recording of Rollin and Tumblin with Little Walter and Muddy Waters remains a notable example of early Chicago blues.

name: Le Moise Roosevelt Graves
description: Blind Roosevelt Graves was a pre-war blues guitarist and singer from Mississippi who recorded both sacred and secular music in the late 1920s and 1930s. His 1929 recording Crazy About My Baby has been cited as possibly the first rock and roll recording, and he made the earliest known version of Guitar Boogie.

name: William Zach Harmon
description: Zac Harmon is an award-winning blues guitarist, singer, and songwriter born and raised in Jackson, Mississippi, whose music continues the lineage of the historic Farish Street blues tradition. He won the International Blues Challenge in 2004 and the Blues Music Award for Best New Artist Debut in 2006, building on decades of experience performing alongside legends like Sam Myers and Z.Z. Hill.

albums.name: Live at Babe and Ricky's Inn
Long As I Got My Guitar

name: King Solomon Hill
description: King Solomon Hill was the recording name of Joe Holmes, a self-taught blues guitarist and singer from McComb, Mississippi, who recorded six songs for Paramount Records in 1932. His recordings feature an eerie falsetto and raw slide guitar played with a cow bone, producing a haunting sound that has captivated blues enthusiasts for decades.

name: Raymond Hill
description: Raymond Hill was an American tenor saxophonist and singer best known as a member of Ike Turner's Kings of Rhythm in the 1950s. He played the celebrated saxophone solo on Rocket 88 (1951), often cited as the first rock and roll record.

albums.name: Sun: The Roots Of Rock Volume 3
Sun: The Roots Of Rock Volume 11

name: Rosa Lee Hill
description: Rosa Lee Hill was a Hill Country blues guitarist and singer born in Como, Mississippi, the daughter of multi-instrumentalist Sid Hemphill. She developed a broody, hypnotic acoustic style characteristic of the north Mississippi tradition, and her songs were recorded by Alan Lomax in 1959.

name: Tony Hollins
description: Tony Hollins was a Delta blues singer, guitarist, and songwriter best known for Crawlin King Snake and Cross Cut Saw Blues, both later popularized by John Lee Hooker. Hollins was a formative influence on Hooker, teaching him guitar and giving him his first instrument.

name: Homemade Jamz Blues Band
description: Homemade Jamz Blues Band is a Tupelo, Mississippi-based blues trio consisting of siblings Ryan, Kyle, and Taya Perry. In 2007 they became the youngest blues band to sign a record deal and have toured extensively across North America and Europe with their authentic Delta-rooted sound.

name: Calvin Jackson
description: Calvin Jackson was a North Mississippi blues drummer considered an innovator in the Hill Country blues style, incorporating elements of the regional fife and drum band tradition into blues band settings. He was the father of Cedric Burnside and performed extensively with R.L. Burnside.

name: Vasti Jackson
description: Vasti Jackson is an American electric blues guitarist, singer, songwriter, and record producer from McComb, Mississippi. He served as musical director and guitarist for legends including Z.Z. Hill, Johnnie Taylor, Little Milton, and Bobby Bland, and played on B.B. King's Grammy-winning album Blues Summit. His 2016 album The Soul of Jimmie Rodgers was nominated for a Grammy Award.

albums.name: Bourbon Street Blues: Live in Nashville

name: Monkey Joe
description: Jesse L. Coleman, known as Monkey Joe, was an American country blues pianist and singer who recorded for Bluebird, Vocalion, and Okeh Records from the 1930s into the 1960s. He worked in juke joints in Jackson, Mississippi during the 1930s and later became a fixture in Chicago blues clubs during the 1960s blues revival.

name: Jimmy Johnson
description: Jimmy Johnson was a celebrated Chicago blues guitarist and singer who moved from Holly Springs, Mississippi to Chicago in 1950. Initially working as a welder, he did not release his first solo album until age 50, but was inducted into the Blues Hall of Fame in 2016 and named Blues Artist of the Year by Living Blues in 2021.

name: Syl Johnson
description: Syl Johnson was an American blues and soul singer, guitarist, and harmonica player who built his career in Chicago after moving from Holly Springs, Mississippi as a teenager. He recorded his most successful material at Hi Records in Memphis including the R&B hit Take Me to the River and the breakbeat classic Different Strokes.

albums.name: Back for a Taste of Your Love

name: Calvin Fuzz Jones
description: Calvin Jones was an American electric blues bassist and singer from Greenwood, Mississippi, best known for his decade-long tenure in Muddy Waters backing band from 1970 to 1980. He co-founded the Legendary Blues Band and appeared in the 1980 film The Blues Brothers performing on Maxwell Street in Chicago.

name: Little Johnny Jones
description: Little Johnny Jones was a Chicago blues pianist and singer best known for his work with Tampa Red, Muddy Waters, and Elmore James. His 1949 recording Big Town Playboy is regarded as a classic of the genre.

albums.name: Live in Chicago with Billy Boy Arnold

name: Willie Kent
description: Willie Kent was an American Chicago blues singer, bassist and songwriter who won the W.C. Handy Award for Best Blues Bassist for ten consecutive years from 1995 to 2004.

name: Willie King
description: Willie King was an Alabama-based blues guitarist, singer, and community activist whose raw, driving blues drew comparisons to Junior Kimbrough and R.L. Burnside. He founded the Freedom Creek Festival and his socially conscious songwriting addressed injustices of life in the rural South.

name: Big Daddy Kinsey
description: Lester Kinsey Jr., known as Big Daddy Kinsey, was a Chicago blues singer, guitarist, and harmonica player who formed The Kinsey Report with his sons. His 1993 album I Am the Blues featured guest appearances from Buddy Guy, James Cotton, and Pinetop Perkins.

name: Ernest Lane
description: Ernest Lane was an American blues pianist from Clarksdale, Mississippi who learned boogie-woogie piano from Pinetop Perkins as a boy alongside his childhood friend Ike Turner. Over six decades he performed with Robert Nighthawk, Willie Dixon, Canned Heat, and the Ike and Tina Turner Revue.

name: Floyd Lee
description: Floyd Lee was an American blues musician born in Lamar, Mississippi who became a founding member of Music Under New York and performed in subway stations in Harlem for nearly 30 years.

name: Bobby Lounge
description: Bobby Lounge (born Dub Brock) is an American blues pianist and singer-songwriter from McComb, Mississippi known for his outrageous barrelhouse piano playing and sardonic songs about Southern life.

albums.name: I Remember the Night Your Trailer Burned Down

name: Mississippi Matilda
description: Mississippi Matilda was an American Delta blues singer and songwriter who recorded four self-penned sides for Bluebird Records in 1936. She is best known for her signature song Hard Working Woman.

name: Lafayette Leake
description: Lafayette Leake was an American blues and jazz pianist, organist, vocalist and composer who played for Chess Records as a session musician, and as a member of the Big Three Trio, during the formative years of Chicago blues. He played piano on many of Chuck Berry's recordings, including the classic original rendition of 'Johnny B. Goode', and was a longtime member of Willie Dixon's Chicago Blues All-Stars.

name: Tommy McClennan
description: Tommy McClennan was an American Delta blues singer and guitarist born in Durant, Mississippi. Known for his rough, energetic playing style, he recorded for Bluebird Records from 1939 to 1942, producing classics like 'Bottle It Up and Go', 'Cross Cut Saw Blues', and 'Whiskey Head Woman'. His songs were later covered by Albert King and Bob Dylan.

name: L. C. McKinley
description: L. C. McKinley was an American Chicago blues guitarist born in Winona, Mississippi, who relocated to Chicago in 1941 and became a regular performer at the 708 Club. He worked as a session musician on recordings mostly in the 1950s, backing artists like Eddie Boyd on the Billboard R&B chart-topping "Five Long Years." His best-known tracks include "Weeping Willow Blues" and "Nit Wit," and his guitar playing was influenced by T-Bone Walker.

name: Hayes McMullan
description: Hayes McMullan was an American Delta blues singer, guitarist and songwriter born in Tallahatchie County, Mississippi. He played alongside Charley Patton in the 1920s before quitting the blues to join a church in the 1930s. His music was preserved through recordings made by musicologist Gayle Dean Wardlow in 1967-68, and his song 'Smoke Like Lightning' later became the Howlin' Wolf classic 'Smokestack Lightnin'.

name: Mississippi Slim
description: Walter Horn Jr., known as Mississippi Slim, was an American blues singer born in Shelby, Mississippi who grew up in Greenville. He moved to Chicago in 1968 where he performed in clubs and became known for his flamboyant stage presence, touring with artists such as Junior Wells. He returned to Mississippi in 1994 and remained active in the blues scene until his death in 2010.

name: McKinley Mitchell
description: McKinley Mitchell was an American Chicago-based blues and rhythm and blues singer who began his career performing gospel music. His 1962 record 'The Town I Live In' became a national R&B hit, peaking at number 8 on the Billboard R&B chart. He recorded for labels including Boxer, One-derful, Chess Records (with Willie Dixon), and Malaco, and was praised by critic Robert Christgau for his soulful style blending Bobby Bland and Brook Benton influences.

name: Sonny Boy Nelson
description: Sonny Boy Nelson, born Eugene Powell, was an American Delta blues musician from Utica, Mississippi who mastered multiple instruments including guitar, banjo, harmonica, mandolin, and violin. He recorded fifteen sides for Bluebird Records in 1936 alongside his wife Mississippi Matilda and members of the Mississippi Sheiks. His acoustic country blues approach was later overshadowed by electric blues styles.

name: Bertha Lee Pate
description: Bertha Lee Pate was an American classic female blues singer active in the 1920s and 1930s, best known as the common-law wife and recording partner of Delta blues legend Charley Patton. She recorded three of her own songs with Patton accompanying her on guitar during his final sessions in 1934. Little else is known of her life beyond these recordings, which remain the only documents of her voice.

name: Dion Payton
description: Dion Payton was an American Chicago blues guitarist and singer born in Greenwood, Mississippi. He gained recording experience at Chess Records with gospel groups before touring with Millie Jackson, Albert King, and O.V. Wright. He assembled the 43rd Street Blues Band in 1985, serving as the weekend house band at Kingston Mines and as Junior Wells's backing band at the Checkerboard Lounge, becoming a legendary figure in Chicago's underground blues scene.

name: Robert Petway
description: Robert Petway was an American Delta blues singer and guitarist who recorded only 16 songs across two sessions for Bluebird Records in Chicago in 1941 and 1942. His composition 'Catfish Blues' became one of the most influential blues songs ever recorded, directly inspiring Muddy Waters' 'Rollin' Stone' and giving the Rolling Stones their name. Despite his enormous influence, virtually nothing is known about his life after his final recording session.

name: Brewer Phillips
description: Brewer Phillips was an American blues guitarist born on a plantation in Coila, Mississippi, who learned the blues from Memphis Minnie at an early age. He is best known as the rhythm guitarist in Hound Dog Taylor's HouseRockers, whose raw two-guitar attack defined Chicago's South Side juke joint sound. After Taylor's death in 1975, Phillips recorded under his own name for Delmark and JSP Records and continued performing with J. B. Hutto and Lil' Ed Williams.

name: Irene Scruggs
description: Irene Scruggs was an American country blues singer, also billed as Chocolate Brown and Dixie Nolan. Born in rural Mississippi and raised in St. Louis, she recorded for Okeh Records starting in 1924 and collaborated with notable musicians including Lonnie Johnson, Blind Blake, and Little Brother Montgomery. She later moved to Europe, settling in Paris and eventually Germany, where she died in 1981.

name: Preston Shannon
description: Preston Shannon was an American electric blues and soul blues guitarist, singer and songwriter, hailed as the reigning 'King of Beale Street' in Memphis. Born in Olive Branch, Mississippi, he relocated to Memphis at age eight and became a fixture on the city's blues scene, known for his powerful guitar work and soulful voice. He released six albums between 1994 and 2014 and was a regular performer at B.B. King's Blues Club on Beale Street.

name: Henry Sloan
description: Henry Sloan was an American musician, one of the earliest figures in the history of Delta Blues. Very little is known for certain about his life, other than that he tutored Charlie Patton in the ways of the blues. He left no known recordings, but both Tommy Johnson and Son House stated that Patton "dogged every step" of Sloan's.

name: Henry Speller
description: Henry Speller was an American Delta blues musician and self-taught visual artist from Panther Burn, Mississippi who spent most of his adult life in Memphis, Tennessee. He played blues guitar and harmonica on Beale Street and performed with Muddy Waters and Howlin' Wolf, who urged him to join his band in Chicago, but Speller declined. His artwork is held in the permanent collections of the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the Smithsonian, and the National Gallery of Art.

name: Houston Stackhouse
description: Houston Stackhouse was an American Delta blues guitarist and singer best known for his association with Robert Nighthawk, whom he taught to play guitar. A key figure in the Mississippi Delta blues scene, he performed on the legendary King Biscuit Time radio program and played alongside Robert Johnson, Sonny Boy Williamson II, and Pinetop Perkins, though he remained largely undiscovered outside the Delta until the blues revival of the late 1960s.

name: Greg "Fingers" Taylor
description: Greg "Fingers" Taylor was an American harmonica player best known for his long tenure with Jimmy Buffett's Coral Reefer Band from 1974 to 2000. Born in Wichita, Kansas and raised in Mississippi, he earned his nickname playing keyboards before taking up harmonica. He released five solo studio albums blending blues, rock, and Gulf Coast sounds, and was nicknamed "The Harpoon Man" for his distinctive harmonica style.

name: James Thomas

albums.name: The Blues Are Alive and Well (1969)

description: James 'Son' Thomas was an American Delta blues guitarist, singer, and sculptor from Eden, Mississippi. A self-taught musician influenced by Arthur 'Big Boy' Crudup, he became known through films by the Center for Southern Folklore in the 1970s and recorded for several small labels. He also gained recognition as a folk artist, creating unfired clay sculptures that reflected his philosophy that 'we all end up in the clay.'

name: Rufus Thomas
description: Rufus C. Thomas, Jr. was an American rhythm-and-blues, funk, soul and blues singer, songwriter, dancer, DJ and comic entertainer from Memphis, Tennessee. Known as "The World's Oldest Teenager," he recorded for Chess, Sun, and Stax Records, producing dance hits like "Walking the Dog" and "Do the Funky Chicken." He embodied the spirit of Memphis music perhaps more than any other artist, serving as mentor, MC, and radio DJ on WDIA across five decades.

name: Shardé Thomas
description: Shardé Thomas is an American fife player in the vanishing American fife and drum blues tradition, and the granddaughter of legendary fife master Othar Turner. She assumed leadership of the Rising Star Fife and Drum Band at age 12 after her grandfather's death in 2003, stepping in to record on Corey Harris's Mississippi to Mali album dedicated to Turner. She plays a homemade cane fife and continues to preserve the North Mississippi hill country fife and drum tradition.

name: Paul Thorn

albums.name: What the Hell Is Goin' On? (2012)

description: Paul Thorn is an American singer-songwriter from Tupelo, Mississippi, whose music blends Southern rock, blues, country, and Americana. Before his music career, he was a professional boxer with a 14-4 record, including a nationally televised bout against Roberto Duran. He has released over a dozen albums, with Don't Let the Devil Ride reaching number one on the Billboard Blues Albums chart.

name: Otha Turner
description: Othar 'Otha' Turner was one of the last well-known practitioners of the vanishing American fife and drum blues tradition, living his entire life as a farmer near Como in northern Mississippi. He led the Rising Star Fife and Drum Band, hosted legendary annual Labor Day goat-roast picnics, and received a National Heritage Fellowship from the NEA in 1992. His track 'Shimmy She Wobble' was featured in Martin Scorsese's 2002 film Gangs of New York.

name: L. C. Ulmer
description: Lee Chester 'L. C.' Ulmer was an American Delta blues musician and multi-instrumentalist from Stringer, Mississippi. A one-man band performer for over half a century, he played at festivals and clubs throughout the Deep South, appeared in the documentaries M for Mississippi (2008) and I Am the Blues (2015), and recorded the album Blues Come Yonder in 2011.

name: Wade Walton
description: Wade Walton was a Delta blues musician and beloved barber from Clarksdale, Mississippi, whose Big Six barbershop became a legendary gathering place for blues musicians. Proficient on guitar, harmonica, and the razor strop, he played with Ike Turner's Kings of Rhythm and counted Howlin' Wolf, Muddy Waters, and Sonny Boy Williamson II among his barbershop patrons. He recorded for Arhoolie and Bluesville Records and was honored with a Mississippi Blues Trail marker.

name: Walter Ward
description: Walter Ward was an American R&B singer and lead vocalist of The Olympics, born in Jackson, Mississippi. He began singing professionally as a child in a gospel group before moving to Los Angeles, where he formed The Olympics and scored a number 8 hit with 'Western Movies' in 1958. His song 'Well (Baby Please Don't Go)' was later recorded by John Lennon during the Imagine sessions.

name: Artie "Blues Boy" White
description: Artie 'Blues Boy' White was an American blues and soul singer born in Vicksburg, Mississippi, who moved to Chicago in 1956 and became one of the foremost Chicago practitioners of Southern Soul music. Known for his flamboyant costumes and stage presence, he headlined the 2000 Chicago Blues Festival and recorded over a dozen albums including collaborations with Little Milton Campbell.

name: Smokey Wilson
description: Robert Lee 'Smokey' Wilson was an American West Coast blues guitarist born in Glen Allan, Mississippi and raised in Lake Village, Arkansas. He moved to Los Angeles in 1970 and opened the Pioneer Club in Watts, where he booked blues greats including Big Joe Turner, Percy Mayfield, and Albert Collins. His down-to-earth Delta-influenced guitar playing earned him international recognition in the 1990s with acclaimed albums on Bullseye Blues.

name: Ike Zimmerman
description: Isaiah 'Ike' Zimmerman was an American Delta blues guitarist who is recognized as Robert Johnson's main guitar teacher. He lived near Beauregard, Mississippi, where Johnson lived with his family for about a year to study guitar, often practicing together in local cemeteries. Though he never recorded commercially, Zimmerman was a highly skilled musician who also played harmonica in local juke joints and lumber camps across Mississippi.

name: Charles Haffer Jr.

albums.name: Strange Things Happening in the Land (1942)

description: Charles Haffer Jr. was a blues and sacred singer recorded by Alan Lomax and Lewis Jones on July 23, 1942, at Nelson's Funeral Home in Clarksdale, Mississippi. His song 'Strange Things Happening in the Land' is a chilling commentary on African-American civil rights, and he also recorded spirituals like 'I'll Be Glad to See the Son When He Comes' and the ballad 'The Titanic' during the same session.

name: Zuzu Bollin

albums.name: Why Don't You Eat Where You Slept Last Night / Matchbox Blues (1951)

description: Zuzu Bollin (born A.D. Bollin) was an American Texas blues guitarist and singer from Frisco, Texas, whose nickname came from Zu Zu ginger snap cookies. He recorded the regional blues classics 'Why Don't You Eat Where You Slept Last Night' and 'Headlight Blues' in 1951 on the Torch label with a band featuring David 'Fathead' Newman and Leroy Cooper, but his career faded until blues enthusiast Chuck Nevitt rediscovered him in 1987. His comeback produced the acclaimed album Texas Bluesman (1989) on Antone's Records, featuring Duke Robillard, and included performances at the Chicago Blues Festival and a European tour before his death from cancer in 1990.

name: David 'Fathead' Newman

albums.name: Fathead: Ray Charles Presents David 'Fathead' Newman (1958)

description: David 'Fathead' Newman was an American jazz and rhythm-and-blues saxophonist best known for his work as a sideman on seminal 1950s and 1960s recordings by Ray Charles. A leading proponent of the 'Texas Tenor' saxophone style, Newman recorded over 38 albums as a leader and played with artists including Aretha Franklin, B.B. King, and Herbie Mann. His soulful, bluesy approach to the tenor saxophone made him one of the most distinctive voices in soul jazz.

name: Roy Brown

albums.name: Good Rocking Tonight: The Best of Roy Brown (1994)

description: Roy Brown (September 10, 1920 – May 25, 1981) was a pioneering American blues shouter whose 1947 recording of his own song "Good Rocking Tonight" is widely cited as one of the records that pointed the way from jump blues toward rock and roll. His impassioned, gospel-inflected vocal delivery and dozens of R&B chart hits for De Luxe Records between 1948 and 1951, including "Hard Luck Blues," made him one of the biggest R&B stars of the era and a direct influence on a generation of singers who followed.

name: Johnny "Guitar" Watson

albums.name: The Very Best of Johnny "Guitar" Watson (1981)

description: John Watson Jr.  (February 3, 1935 – May 17, 1996), often known professionally as Johnny "Guitar" Watson, was an American musician.  A flamboyant showman and electric guitarist in the style of T-Bone Walker, his recording career spanned 40 years, and encompassed rhythm and blues, funk and soul music.

name: Robert Pete Williams
description: Robert Pete Williams (March 14, 1914 – December 31, 1980) was an American Louisiana blues musician. His music characteristically employed unconventional structures and guitar tunings, and his songs are often about the time he served in prison. His song "I've Grown So Ugly" has been covered by Captain Beefheart, on his album Safe as Milk (1967), and by The Black Keys, on Rubber Factory (2004).

name: Geeshie Wiley

albums.name: Mississippi Masters: Early American Blues Classics 1927-35 (1994)

description: Geeshie Wiley was an American country blues singer and guitar player who recorded six songs for Paramount Records, issued on three records in April 1930. According to the blues historian Don Kent, Wiley "may well have been the rural South's greatest female blues singer and musician". Little is known of her life, and there are no known photographs of her.

name: Ruth Brown

albums.name: Rockin' in Rhythm: The Best of Ruth Brown (1996)
Miss Rhythm: The Rest & More of the Best (1997)
Mama, He Treats Your Daughter Mean and Other Hits (1997)
Blues & Rhythm Series: The Chronological Ruth Brown 1949-1950 (2001)

description: Ruth Alston Brown (née Weston; January 12, 1928 – November 17, 2006) was an American singer-songwriter and actress, sometimes referred to as the "Queen of R&B".  She was noted for bringing a pop music style to R&B music in a series of hit songs for Atlantic Records in the 1950s, such as "So Long", "Teardrops from My Eyes" and "(Mama) He Treats Your Daughter Mean".  For these contributions, Atlantic became known as "the house that Ruth built" (alluding to the popular nickname for the old Yankee Stadium).

name: Rick Estrin
description: Rick Estrin is an American blues harmonica player and vocalist known for his sharp, witty songwriting and slick, sophisticated harmonica style rooted in the Chicago tradition of Little Walter and Sonny Boy Williamson II. As a teenager he moved to Chicago, where he learned firsthand from South Side blues veterans, before returning to California and fronting Little Charlie & the Nightcats for thirty years and later Rick Estrin & The Nightcats. He has won multiple Blues Music Awards, including for Best Instrumentalist–Harmonica, and his song "My Next Ex-Wife" won Song of the Year in 1994.

name: Larry Davis
description: Larry Davis was an American Texas and soul blues singer, guitarist, and bassist best known for writing (with Joseph Scott) and originally recording "Texas Flood" in 1958 for Duke Records, a song later made famous by Stevie Ray Vaughan. He began his career as a drummer before switching to bass, played in Albert King's band and absorbed King's guitar style, and partnered in the mid-1950s with guitarist Fenton Robinson, who played guitar on the original "Texas Flood" session. After a 1972 motorcycle accident sidelined him for years, Davis staged a comeback in the 1980s, winning four W.C. Handy Awards in 1982.

name: Denise LaSalle

albums.name: On the Loose / Trapped by a Thing Called Love (1992)
My Toot Toot - The Definitive Anthology (2003)
Making A Good Thing Better - The Complete Westbound Singles 1970-76 (2013)

description: Denise LaSalle was a Mississippi-born singer-songwriter who became one of the leading voices of Southern soul-blues, scoring a number-one R&B hit with "Trapped by a Thing Called Love" in 1971. A prolific songwriter as much as a performer, she signed with Malaco Records in the early 1980s and penned hits for labelmates including Z.Z. Hill, helping define the label's deep soul-blues sound alongside artists like Bobby "Blue" Bland and Little Milton. Following the death of Koko Taylor in 2009, LaSalle was widely hailed as the new "Queen of the Blues" and was inducted into the Blues Hall of Fame in 2011.

name: Peppermint Harris

albums.name: Lonesome as I Can Be: The Jewel Recordings (2001)

description: Peppermint Harris (born Harrison D. Nelson Jr.) was a Texas blues singer and guitarist who began performing around Houston in the late 1940s, often accompanied by his friend and fellow Texan Lightnin' Hopkins. He scored a number-one R&B hit in 1951 with 'I Got Loaded' on Aladdin Records, a jump blues classic that became his signature song and was later covered by numerous artists. Harris kept recording into the 1990s across labels in Houston, Louisiana, California, and New Jersey, leaving a lasting mark on postwar Texas jump blues.

name: Eddie "Cleanhead" Vinson

albums.name: The Blues Collection: Eddie Vinson, Cleanhead Blues (1995)
Blues, Boogie & Bebop - Meat's Too High (1998)
Blues & Rhythm Series: The Chronological Eddie Vinson 1945-1947 (2001)

description: Eddie "Cleanhead" Vinson (December 18, 1917 - July 2, 1988) was an American jump blues alto saxophonist and blues shouter from Houston, Texas, nicknamed for a lye-straightening mishap that left him bald. He scored R&B hits such as "Kidney Stew Blues" and "Old Maid Boogie" with his own big band in the late 1940s (a young John Coltrane briefly played in its sax section), and he blended gutbucket blues vocals with bebop-inflected horn playing throughout his career. After a comeback via the Johnny Otis Revue in the 1960s-70s, he remained a vital live and recording presence into the 1980s, including a celebrated pairing with the swing-revival band Roomful of Blues.

name: Cedell Davis
description: CeDell Davis was a Delta blues guitarist and singer from Helena, Arkansas whose sound was reshaped by childhood polio, which left his fretting hand unable to form conventional chords; he adapted by dragging a butter knife across the strings, producing a dissonant, clattering slide style that critic Robert Palmer described as 'a welter of metal-stress harmonic transients.' Davis spent roughly a decade playing bass and guitar in Robert Nighthawk's band around Helena before a 1957 police raid left him paralyzed from the waist down, confining him to a wheelchair for the rest of his life. Rediscovered by Palmer in the 1990s, he recorded a series of raw, unconventional albums for Fat Possum Records that made him a cult figure of the hill country blues revival.

name: Chris Cain
description: Chris Cain is a San Jose, California guitarist, singer, and songwriter whose fluid, jazz-inflected soloing and smoky baritone voice made him one of the leading West Coast blues stylists to emerge in the late 1980s. His 1987 debut album 'Late Night City Blues' earned four Blues Music Award nominations, including Guitarist of the Year, launching a recording career that spanned Blind Pig, Blue Rock-It, and Alligator Records. Mentored in his youth by B.B. King and Albert King, whose influence shaped his singing and playing, Cain in turn became a touchstone for younger guitarists such as Joe Bonamassa, who has called him one of his favorite players.

name: Otis Clay

albums.name: Trying to Live My Life Without You (1972)

description: Otis Clay (1942–2016) was a Mississippi-born, Chicago-based soul and blues singer whose gospel-rooted, deep-soul voice made him one of the great soul blues stylists of the postwar era. Backed by Willie Mitchell and the Hi Rhythm Section, he cut the deep-soul classics "Trying to Live My Life Without You" and "I Can't Take It" for Hi Records in the 1970s, songs that became blues and soul standards later covered by Bob Seger and Ann Peebles among others. He remained a fixture on the blues and soul circuit for decades, recording for Blind Pig and Alligator-affiliated labels, was inducted into the Blues Hall of Fame in 2013, and continued performing gospel and blues shows in Chicago until his death.

name: Michael Burks
description: Michael Burks (1957-2012) was an American electric blues guitarist and singer raised in Camden, Arkansas, where his father's friendship with Albert King gave the young Burks direct exposure to King's stinging, string-bending guitar style. Burks fused that Albert King foundation with the fire of Jimi Hendrix and Freddie King to create a hard-edged, rock-tinged blues sound, releasing acclaimed albums like "I Smell Smoke" (2003) and "Iron Man" (2008) on Alligator Records. Widely regarded as one of the most powerful blues-rock guitarists of his generation, he earned multiple Blues Music Award nominations before his sudden death in 2012.

name: Jack Owens

albums.name: It Must Have Been the Devil (1971)

description: Jack Owens was a Bentonia, Mississippi bluesman who spent most of his life farming, selling bootleg liquor, and running a weekend juke joint rather than pursuing a professional recording career. Alongside his neighbor Skip James, he was a leading exponent of the eerie, minor-key 'Bentonia School' of Delta blues, though he sang in his natural voice rather than James's falsetto and used his own guitar tunings. Not recorded until he was rediscovered by musicologist David Evans in 1966, Owens went on to record for Testament and Albatross Records, tour blues festivals in the US and Europe with harmonica player Bud Spires, and receive a 1993 National Heritage Fellowship.
